design:
D1. Links are removed before the worktree, never followed: every removal path in worktrees.py first walks the worktree (os.scandir, not following links) and unlinks each symlink or junction (os.path.islink, or st_file_attributes & FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT on Windows), then runs git worktree remove --force; the rmtree fallback uses the same walk. One helper, used by all five removal sites.
D2. The Hub makes the links itself. _symlink_shared_dependencies (worktrees.py:311) covers SHARED_DEPENDENCY_DIRS at the root only (worktrees.py:65), so hub/ui/node_modules was never linked and agents made junctions by hand. It now also links node_modules beside each tracked package.json up to three levels deep, and on OSError from symlink_to creates a directory junction (junctions need no privilege on NTFS). A failure of both is still reported as today (F567).
D3. A mend gets its own scratch checkout (operator, 2026-10-27), created for the mend and removed in a finally block, so the mender's checkout never moves and an abandoned mend leaves nothing behind.
D4. 'Never chosen' and 'nothing merges' are told apart by a settings event: the operator clearing main_branch is recorded, and _adopt_detected_main_branch (api/v1/projects.py:374) adopts only when no settings event ever set or cleared it.

open_questions.question: Should the Hub fall back to a junction when a symlink is refused? Operator 2026-10-27: yes (requirement dependencies-linked-without-symlink-rights).
Mend in a separate scratch checkout, or switch the mender's checkout back afterwards? Operator 2026-10-27: a separate scratch checkout (requirement mend-in-a-scratch-checkout).

problem:
F1038 (severity B): an agent linked hub/ui/node_modules into its task worktree with a junction; when the Hub removed that worktree, `git worktree remove --force` followed the junction and emptied the main checkout's hub/ui/node_modules, twice in 20 minutes on 2026-10-23. Every removal path in hub/hub/worktrees.py (lines 1032, 1237, 1557, 1611, 1671) and the rmtree fallback follow links. A link can point anywhere, so the loss is not limited to regenerable dependencies.

Mender (vault src-945b5f2468b8): a mend commits on `mend/<task-id>` (task_transition_service.py:1346) in the mender's own checkout and never switches it back, so the next delivery is refused with "not the registered git worktree for refs/heads/agentweave/mender", which misnames the cause: the directory is registered, just on another branch. The operator had to switch it back by hand.

F1016 (severity B): emptying Settings -> Integration -> Main branch means "nothing merges", but reopening the folder runs `_adopt_detected_main_branch` (api/v1/projects.py:374), which writes the detected branch over the empty value, records no settings event, and then merges approved work that was waiting.

requirements.rationale: Agents create junctions themselves (DEAD-ENDS documents `mklink /J` for running vitest in a worktree), and a link may point at a shared .venv or the vault, so the Hub cannot assume it only removes its own links or only regenerable data.
requirements.statement: Removing any worktree the Hub created leaves unchanged the contents of every directory that a symbolic link or junction inside that worktree points to, whoever created the link.

requirements.rationale: Making removal safe by skipping it would leave the stranded checkouts that F693 and the mender bug already show block later turns.
requirements.statement: A worktree that contains links is still fully removed and deregistered from git, as one without links is.

requirements.rationale: Today every successful mend disables the mender until the operator switches its checkout back by hand.
requirements.statement: After a mend has been committed and merged, the mender's next turn starts in its own checkout on `agentweave/mender` without any manual git action.

requirements.rationale: The present message sends the operator to delete a directory that only needs switching.
requirements.statement: When an agent's own workspace is a registered worktree on a branch other than the agent's own and the Hub cannot safely switch it back, the refusal names the branch it is on and the branch expected, and does not say the directory is not a registered worktree.

requirements.rationale: An empty value today means both 'never chosen' and the operator's 'nothing merges'; the Hub overwrites the second as if it were the first.
requirements.statement: A main branch the operator has explicitly cleared stays cleared when the project's folder is opened again, and no approved task merges as a result of reopening.
When the Hub sets a project's main branch on its own (adopting a detected branch on first registration), it records a settings event naming the old and new values, as an operator change does.

requirements.rationale: On this machine every symlink is refused (F567), so no turn gets node_modules or .venv and agents create junctions by hand; a Hub-made link is one the Hub knows to remove safely, and the per-turn notice stops.
requirements.statement: When the Hub prepares a checkout and a dependency directory exists in the main checkout (node_modules, .venv or venv at the root, or node_modules beside a tracked package.json up to three directories deep, such as hub/ui/node_modules), it links that directory into the checkout, using a directory junction where the platform refuses a symbolic link, and the turn carries no 'could not be linked' notice for it.

requirements.rationale: Operator decision 2026-10-27: a separate checkout also covers a mend abandoned half-way, which switching back afterwards does not.
requirements.statement: A mend is built in a separate scratch checkout that is removed afterwards, whether the mend lands or is abandoned; the mender's own checkout is never switched to the mend branch.

in_scope: Every path by which the Hub removes a worktree it created (task, review, agent and scratch checkouts), including fallbacks
The mend path and the preparation of the mender's own workspace for its next turn
The refusal message when an agent's registered worktree is on an unexpected branch
Reopening a project whose main branch the operator cleared
Linking the project's dependency directories (root and nested, e.g. hub/ui/node_modules) into a Hub-created checkout, with a junction when a symlink is refused
non_goals: Recovering files already lost to F1038
Changing what 'nothing merges' means or how approval skips merging while it is set
Installing dependencies into a worktree that the main checkout does not have

summary: Three defects where the Hub's handling of checkouts and the merge target damages or overrides something it does not own, and the gap that caused the worst of them: removing a worktree empties whatever a link inside it points to (F1038), a mend leaves the mender's own checkout on the mend branch so every later mender turn is refused, an operator's "nothing merges" is silently replaced by the detected branch when the folder is reopened (F1016), and on a machine that cannot create symlinks the Hub links no dependency directory at all, so agents make junctions by hand (how F1038 happened). The Hub now links dependencies itself, falling back to a junction, and removes links without following them.
